traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: DELTA Phyllanthaceae (read 2026-10-16): spiral or distichous. 'distichous usually' is my weighting: Phyllanthus (~1,200 spp.) bears two-ranked leaves on flattened leafy branchlets.

traits.perianth.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) p. 260, 261: flowers unisexual, petals generally smaller than the sepals or absent (general formula K2-8, C0 or 3-9). A sepal-only flower is mapped to 'tepals'.

traits.flower_merosity.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) p. 261: perianth mostly 5-merous, sometimes 3- to 9-merous.

traits.stamens.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) p. 260: Ronse De Craene general formula: stamens 2 to 35, one whorl usually alternating with the petals.

traits.carpels.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) p. 260, 261: carpels 3 or 2, always 3 in 5-merous flowers; general formula 1 to 15.

traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 133 Euphorbiaceae, which holds what APG sets apart as Phyllanthaceae (Phyllanthus, Bridelia, Antidesma, Aporosa, Baccaurea, Hymenocardia, the genera with paired ovules): leaves alternate, simple, mostly with stipules; flowers unisexual, the sexes on one plant or on two; petals mostly absent; ovary superior, of three cells; fruit a capsule or a drupe (Baccaurea's a berry). Library 1.0's family is 82% trees and shrubs. The ovary's place and the berry are inferred, not traced.
